# Resource: stripe_webhook_endpoint

An endpoint Stripe sends events to. The signing `secret` is returned once, at creation, and is kept in state as a sensitive value. `terraform destroy` deletes the endpoint.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_webhook_endpoint" "events" {
  url            = "https://example.com/stripe/webhook"
  enabled_events = ["invoice.paid", "customer.subscription.deleted"]
}

# The signing secret is sensitive and set once, when the endpoint is created.
output "webhook_signing_secret" {
  value     = stripe_webhook_endpoint.events.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `enabled_events` - (Required) The list of events to enable for this endpoint. You may specify `['*']` to enable all events, except those that require explicit selection.
* `url` - (Required) The URL of the webhook endpoint.

The following arguments are optional:

* `api_version` - (Optional) Events sent to this endpoint will be generated with this Stripe Version instead of your account's default Stripe Version. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `connect` - (Optional) Whether this endpoint should receive events from connected accounts (`true`), or from your account (`false`). Defaults to `false`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `description` - (Optional) An optional description of what the webhook is used for.
* `disabled` - (Optional) Disable the webhook endpoint if set to true.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `application` - The ID of the associated Connect application.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `secret` - (Sensitive) The endpoint's secret, used to generate [webhook signatures](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/signatures). Only returned at creation.
* `status` - The status of the webhook. It can be `enabled` or `disabled`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a webhook endpoint using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_webhook_endpoint.events
  id = "we_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_webhook_endpoint.events
  identity = {
    id = "we_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the webhook endpoint.

Using `terraform import`, import a webhook endpoint using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_webhook_endpoint.events we_123
```

~> An imported endpoint has no `secret`, because Stripe returns it only at creation. Stripe does not return `disabled` or `connect`, so an imported webhook endpoint has them null: a configuration that sets `disabled` plans an update after the import, and one that sets `connect` plans a replacement.
